How many Muslims live in those villages? In those areas of Kljuc municipality there are about 12 and a half thousand Muslims and they represent more than 70 per cent of the total population. Let me also say that in this area, there are about 4.300 members of the Serbian nationality and that they should have represented the Bosnian municipality of Kljuc as the SDA and MBO deputies -- as they call themselves, the Muslim national block -- already in December were the only ones in Bosnia-Herzegovina to declare a Bosnian Muslim municipality of Kljuc. What was the result of the activities of our police and the Army of the Serbian Republic of BH? The operations were carried out energetically. And in a very short period of time of a few hours, the units were broken up. Most of the members surrendered with -- some with small arms, others with automatic weapons. Some 20 to 30 per cent of the most extreme withdrew and continued operating in the areas of Sanica and Sanski Most municipality, which were still in their hands and according to some reports a part tried to reach the municipality of Prijedor and Bihac. Many houses have been destroyed. The population has fled. Many have been captured. The newly-built mosque has been destroyed which officially had not been opened yet. Nevertheless the Serbian army and police hit only the houses from which resistance was put up. The new mosque in Velagici, or rather Pudin Han, was one of the largest Muslim strongholds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. I should like to point out that it is not true that the mosque was a fierce stronghold of our men. They just needed a pretext to destroy all sacral buildings of Muslim and Catholic faith. So 17 mosques were destroyed in Kljuc and one Catholic church. So this was just a pretext for them to destroy religious buildings. To this day the Orthodox church in Kljuc is intact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] In Krasulje, Gornji and Donji Sanica, Plamenica, Prhovo, and Ramici, during the mopping-up operations, other buildings were also destroyed but much less than in Velagici and Pudin Han. What about other Muslim villages? With the exception of parts of villages where ambushes were organised and where members of the Muslim Territorial Defence and the Green Berets set up ambushes, we did not engage in any other operations. In the town of Kljuc and the surrounding villages, such as Dubocani and others, inhabited exclusively by Muslims, there was no destruction nor was a single shot fired in those areas, because in these areas the population had not been ideologically indoctrinated, that is, the Muslim population. And where there was no resistance, we did not have to carry out any destruction. Quite a large quantity of weaponry has been confiscated. What kind of evidence do you have, what proof of all the -- of the SDA activities and their ring leaders? This is only a part of the confiscated objects which provides evidence that they organised --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask the Court to wind back the tape, where the chief of police, Vinko Kondic, says that they engaged in an organised fashion in their defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which part would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe a couple of seconds back only. While Vinko was speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop here and -- okay. We can start playing from here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters be assisted with the page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are ring leaders. This is just a part of the confiscated material which documents that they organised defence. There you have Vinko Kondic who says that we organised our defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I heard the interpreter request the page of the transcript. It's page 4 of the English. I don't know what it is in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I think in all fairness it should be pointed out that right after Mr. Kondic says, "It's shows that they had organised defence," he says "and prepared themselves to undertake aggressive combat activities at the most suitable moment for them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. Let's continue with the recording. The technicians, please. We'll continue from where we stopped. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] They chose a favourable moment for combat activities. Regarding the political and security situation, we drew attention to all the problems appearing in the territory of Kljuc municipality, so that the location of units is given in the municipality of Kljuc, the positions of the former Yugoslav People's Army, their axis of withdrawal, their activities in certain localities, then also assessments of the security situation are indicative of the difficult position of the Muslims in certain regions. Then they use the old assessments that certain areas are traditionally Chetnik strongholds. And their overall indoctrination was such to use propaganda that there was no life for them in this area. But the inhabitants of these villages should not be misled to believe that the Serbs are naive. It is known that some weapons are still concealed and it would be best for them to hand it over as soon as possible. The sooner they do so, the better, because for as long as they have weapons, there is a potential danger of war spreading to these villages. Let this programme be an appeal for them to surrender their weapons as soon as possible so that they may live in these areas for years -- hundreds of years ahead, because otherwise it is quite clear what can happen, because the Serbs nowhere on this planet and least of all in Kljuc have reason to beg anyone for anything. During the performance of combat operations in this area, the members of the Army of Republika Srpska and members of certain units established full control, and in these areas there were no -- there was no significant fighting nor attempts to control certain areas. These were more individual exchanges of fire by fanatics who still remained in the woods. They did not wish to surrender. But from one day to the next there are more and more people who have surrendered. That people had this in mind long ago is illustrated by an example. Before the Second World War a large number of Croats lived in the village of Velagici. Since from 1941 to 1945 almost all able-bodied men were in the army of the independent state of Croatia, there was no going back. They sold their houses and property after their war and moved away. However, not a single house was sold to a Serb by a Croat from Velagici. They all sold their houses to Muslims. And there were examples that the Serbs made them better offers. The second example: At the right side along the asphalt road to Velagici and Pudin Han, looking from the direction of Kljuc, there was not a single house. Pursuant to orders given by the higher authorities - we know by whom - several houses have recently been built on that side. They were bit on the slopes so that it would be easy for them to observe the road and block it when the need occurred. The third example is even more typical: Muslims, too, following the example of their allies, Croats, slaughtered their neighbour, a Croat, in Velagici because he had decided to stay and did not want to commit crimes against the Serbs. Can you imagine what a great hero Asim Egrlic was from the village of Egrlic of the same name, just of Kljuc. He was the President of the municipal SDA. It's best shown by the fact that he injured himself at a barricade and he couldn't run away, as his brother did, and the Serbs know where his brother is hiding. What is the organisational military structure of the Green Berets and the MBO and who is in their leadership? What kind of evidence is there available? In the region of Kljuc municipality, we managed to prove through operational work that there was a bond between the official leadership of the SDA and the Muslim Bosniak Party, the party, the organisation, and that the leaders of these parties were directly involved in the procurement of weapons, in the establishment of units, and that the whole process was organised and realised through political parties. Were they well armed in this area? According to the information available to us from before, there were no significant quantities of weapons in Kljuc. That was explained in the material that we seized and found, as well as in the operational processing of each particular case. Our assessment is that in the Kljuc municipality in various types of formations they had between 1300 and 1500 men and an appropriate quantity of weapons. However, there was a quantity of weapons legally possessed, that is, hunting weapons, pistols, et cetera. The rest, the illegally held weapons that we discovered and requisitioned, some 60 per cent of, are the weapons probably seized from the Serbian Army Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Your Honours, you can see here what kind of weapons they were, old-fashioned Kuburas [phoen]. Rifles. You can look for yourself, as if this kind of weapons can hurt a military force. Here you have proof what kind of weapons were involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Filipovic, it's quite difficult to see on the picture. Can you just show us what sort of a weapon it was by -- I'm not sure you can, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are what we call Kuburas. Medieval fighters had such weapons. You put one bullet in. Then you fire it. One could get killed ten times in the meantime before putting in the second bullet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we can just make out -- yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Let's have a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a very short rewind, going back to when -- to the moment that cache of weapons is being shown, just a couple of seconds I would imagine. A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to rewind a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause there for a moment. Can we pause for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are we -- do you know what we're looking at there, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There's the word "Zastava" there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Looks like some amazing contraption on top, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. There was definitely a rifle that I could see before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a box. In Serbia there was a factory of weapons called "Zastava." And I claim with full responsibility that we didn't have a single box of weapons. This is a JNA document. JNA was supplied with Zastavas, weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. We can continue playing the tape, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can just hear some amazing noises. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. That's a printer, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. Can we just continue for a moment to the next, where we see the other weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] A number of the members of the units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what we can see to the right-hand part of the screen? One can just make out what looks like some kind of a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Perhaps we can continue playing now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] We will come to these automatic, semi-automatic weapons, different types of rifles, bombs, and some mortars. In one of the seized -- the documents it says that the Muslims in Kljuc were allegedly in danger. In Sanski Most, while the triage hospital would be situated in Hripavci. As for the danger for Muslims is concerned, let me mention that it was up to this last war, was that the Muslims owned most of the trade companies and shops here in Kljuc. They owned restaurants, bakers' shops, jewellery stores, garages, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Stop. I would like to point to Your Honours that Muslims were workers. They worked there where money was generated in bakeries and mechanic shops, unlike the Serbs who were in leadership bodies. And when they say the Muslims were rich, it is true that they were richer than the Serbs in the Kljuc municipality. But we can say that they earned this through their own efforts and work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We may -- can continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] In the municipality we can say that there were more mosques than Orthodox churches.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause, please. Pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pause. Pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop the film. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who that is, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovo Banjac, president of the municipal assembly and president of the Crisis Staff, commander or president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before -- he appears to be wearing some kind of a military uniform here. Before your --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. He is wearing a military uniform, a JNA military uniform, of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before your arrest in May, on the 28th of May, did you see Mr. Banjac wearing this type of military uniform at all?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was wearing civilian clothes. He was a fat person and it was difficult for him to find proper clothing. But when the situation got tense, he was in a great hurry to procure a JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. If we could carry on playing the film. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] In the municipality of Kljuc we did not suspend a single Muslim director before that nor did we have any intention. Are you saying that up to the war, up to May 27, the Muslims had more directors than they should have proportionally in respect to the population size? They had many directors, as were legally elected in institutions. In the old government, during the old government we did not wish to replace them, we wanted everything to be as it should normally be in peacetime. The same as the Croat television TV Sarajevo, has become a huge factory of lies. How far they are ready to go is best shown in an example taken from Kljuc. Alija Izetbegovic congratulated Omer Filipovic by means of TV Sarajevo on allegedly taking over the town on the Sana River accomplished by the Green Berets. To make the victory complete and to arouse hopes of enraged and hopeless Alija's combatants who fought the holy jihad in Sarajevo and other front lines in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic tried even harder by congratulating Filipovic for the arrest of more than 4.000 Serbo-Chetniks. I'm using this opportunity to mention the abominable lies created in the factory of lies spread by HTV, Sarajevo TV and radio, in which they broadcast news that Muslim extremists led by Omer Filipovic, the commander of the Territorial Defence of the so-called Bosnia and Herzegovina, took over Kljuc and arrested several thousand Serbo-Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we just --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was about to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was Ljuban Bajic. I spoke of him yesterday. He was so clever that my brother had to do his graduation papers for him in order for him to become professor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Having heard that, let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Not only in the area controlled by the forces and the military units. These are also lies. You can convince yourself of this. I think you can establish -- you can see the reputable Muslims and talk to them, and you'll make sure that these are notorious lies, that there were no massacres, imprisonment, killing of Muslims in the Kljuc municipality. Those are rumours that allegedly Filipovic and Egrlic was killed, and apart from them also Omer Zubcevic, a dentist from Kljuc. They are in Kljuc safe and sound, although Filipovic knows very well and we publicly state to his supporters to open their eyes and to open the eyes of all the Muslims who follow him, a toast to his health, and Omer Filipovic heard this in prison somewhere because already on 28th of May, only a day after the outbreak of the war in the area of Velagici and Pudin Han he has been led away by the Army of the Serbian Republic of B and H and he has no clue of the alleged arrest of the 4.000 Serbs. It is true that rather a lot of Muslim extremists were captured during the cleansing of Velagici, Pudin Han, Krasulje, and here we found -- Omer Filipovic had complete lists of the composition of the Crisis and War Staff were found, as well as of the military structure of the Green Berets and who should be liquidated in Kljuc and where to get arms. Most of the members of the Crisis Staff have been arrested, they namely had a Crisis Staff and a War Staff. The War Staff was commanded by Omer Filipovic, coordinators in the field were Amir Avdic and Nedzad Djeric. And Asim Egrlic was responsible for political matters. The first three are JNA reserve officers. Filipovic is a lieutenant. He was brought in as commander and arrested together with Asim Egrlic who has been wounded and on the first day in the course of the combat actions he was brought in as well. The president of the Party of Democratic Action was brought in. The other is president of the MBO party. Avdic and Djeric are still on the run and they constitute the harshest most extreme part of the Green Berets in the Kljuc municipality. The Crisis Staff was composed somewhat more broadly. It consisted of Asim Egrlic, Omer Filipovic, Iksan Zukanovic, Suad Mesic, Ibrahim Egrlic, Muhamed Filipovic, and a certain number of couriers and drivers, which is not that -- their number is not so important. Most of the Crisis Staff members have been brought in as well and are being operatively check on, so we will establish the individual part of the responsibility in the participation of everyone together with the military investigative authorities. It is characteristic that in this area also workshops were found in which the Muslims manufactured old-fashioned pistols and mortars. The master craftsmen were Muhamed Konjevic from Sanica, Cazim Medanovic and others and the workshop was found in Dubocani. All this shows that the Muslims in the Kljuc municipality have been preparing themselves for the war with the Serbs for a long time, that they planned everything as if they had not known that the Serbs can fare well as well, especially when defending their hearths and home soil. But a few Muslim, women, children, and elderly men who remained in Velagici and Pudin Han are in great distress for lack of food. Therefore, they started to steal victuals from each other. The best proof for this is the example that they are already coming to the police at the checkpoint to report thefts. Regarding the situation in these wartime circumstances, everything is fine. But some women from Velagici and Gornji Vojici have been complaining the thefts of even flour, salt, and oil. Do you have any concrete names who came, who reported such things? I do. This morning a woman came complaining. Her name is Bida Halilovic from Gornji Vojici. Well, but yesterday evening at half past 7 here is a witness in the village who saw candles burning at half past 7 from here house. Things were stolen she had received the day before from her daughter -- sister-in-law. So she and her four or five little young children could survive. Flour, oil, and the like were stolen. They saw lights in the night and they didn't dare to go out. And in other words -- well, the other woman under suspicion is she a Muslim? Also a Muslim. And the theft as well. They are stealing amongst themselves. Who now remained here in Velagici? Do you mean from us? From them. The Muslims that is. Only women and young children are left and the occasional grown-up man who has not been under suspicion and released. Where are the others? The others, most of them fled into the woods. A few of them have been -- When the fighting started in Velagici and Pudin Han, by the plan of the Green Berets, war should have spread to the town of Kljuc. Therefore, the Muslim extremists opened fire from the nearby hill of Hamlovici, from the top of the Egrlici and from the new Luka housing area, but the Serbian defenders were prepared and neutralised them quickly. The hardest resistance came from the mosque and the Catholic church in town from a stable at Hamlovici when the fire was neutralised Muhamed Filipovic, called Maho, and Ago Sahatlic and his son were brought in almost 10.000 medical syringes and a major quantity of bandages were found which was intended for the Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to ask to stop anyhow because I want to ask Mr. Filipovic about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In addition, I would have thought that the interpreter is going need a break with the speed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As soon as we finish this, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much more is there?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to ask -- there's another six or seven pages. Part of it is irrelevant, I think, Your Honour. I'll come back to what Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, ask the question and then we'll break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you've heard an allegation there that there was resistance at the mosque and the Catholic church in town and something about a fire. And that's -- after that you were brought in. Can you tell us whether there's anything -- any truth in this.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there is no truth in this. When I said "stop," I intended to say this. When they mentioned fire, this happened at 5.30 on the 28th, when we were taken to Stara Gradiska. At the moment when we were taken down the police steps, firing started from that area and then we were pushed into the police station quickly because they said that the Green Berets were attacking. The answer was a logical answer to this. One had to find an excuse for 22 persons to be captured and taken to prison and to say that they were captured during the fighting and this was not the case. They said that Mahmut Filipovic had 10.000 syringes. This is not true. He was head of a surgery, of a laboratory in the health centre. And material was -- he issued material, medical material. Mahmut Filipovic has nothing to do with that. But one went so far as to blame everyone. I claim with responsibility that there was no firing by the Muslims from the mosque and Catholic church. Only the birds could approach that area, with the exception, of course, of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, then before the break, if Your Honour goes -- I don't know whether it's possible for the video people to just skip that. There's a whole lot -- a bit about sugar, at page 17 -- sorry, fish, not sugar. I really don't think it's necessary to go through that. It's on page 17 of the transcript. And the -- roughly the counter is 57.45. Your Honour, I've checked -- the other thing is -- I knew I'd seen a document unhelpfully I'm not sure it's dated, but I think we can date it. It's Exhibit P923 -- I'm sorry, P984, which is a report that at 3.00 a.m. the mosque in Kljuc was blown up. It's -- on the index it says July 1st. I'm not sure why, but it can be dated in that they were discussing the municipal assembly meeting for the first time again, and that was July of 1992. So it's -- it's June/July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So let's have a 15-minute break now, resuming at just after half past 5.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before we continue with the video, can we just confirm with Mr. Filipovic that the person they're talking about here is somebody called Mahmud Filipovic and not you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't quite get this, Ms. Korner. The person ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In that part where we stopped the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Page 11 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought that Mr. Filipovic was saying this was someone called Mahmud Filipovic and not him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mention is made of Mahmut, with a "T" at the end, Filipovic. Mahmut, with a "T."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's not you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If we carry on with the video, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Adequate measures were taken against all captured persons, interrogations, and all information which was available before to the public security organs so that not against a single one of the members of these parties, the SDA, such measures were taken as could be heard in the media. Is it correct that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw the name of this man in Cyrillic on the subtitles, but can you just tell us -- confirm who that is.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the subtitle give his position?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't watching, but he's wearing an olive-green shirt of the JNA. But he was commander or chief of the Territorial Defence. If you wind it back, we'll see. But I didn't pay attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just so that we can confirm for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go back to the subtitle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop. And then run it forward again, please, and then pause to where we can see the subtitle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Chief of Staff of the 17th Brigade. That is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But before the outbreak of the war, he was in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We can -- sorry, if we carry on, please, playing the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] So that information that was already available to the public security organs, so that not against a single one of the members of these parties, that is, the SDA, were measures taken as could be heard in the media. Is it correct that Egrlic and Filipovic were captured and that there are proceedings against them? It is correct that they have been captured, that they are in custody, and that proceedings will be taken against them by the competent organs. What is your message to the extremist group still hiding around in the woods? The extremist groups will finally be forced to surrender and to surrender their weapons, otherwise they will not stand a chance. So it's better for them to do that right away? The sooner the better. The lesser the consequences for them. How far Muslim lies go is shown by these examples. Sarajevo Radio and TV and the HTV have been broadcasting information that allegedly the Serbs executed all distinguished Muslims in Kljuc. Other Western media are carrying these reports. They speak of many examples. This is best disproved by the following recordings and words: "Now, look, I do not know what to say --"

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this man? Can you tell us his name from the subtitle?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him personally. It is Omer Zubcevic, a dentist in the Kljuc health centre. He was not in the Manjaca camp. They're interviewing him here, and you can imagine what the interview is like. He was told what he should say and then filmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that he was told what he should say?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so, as I was told in Manjaca. I would be taken to the interrogator after being beaten up, and then I'd have to answer questions. So I assume he, too, was threatened. If you want to remain alive, say ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We can carry on playing the video. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] As for their attitude towards me, our presence here tells everything. Nobody ever used any force or anything. We are really delighted here. And they helped us and offered us whatever we might need because -- because of shortages of foodstuffs and such things, we can't get hold of them. They offered us all that. So I'm speechless. I don't know what else to say. You see me here sound and well. So the official authorities have treated you absolutely normally? Totally. They asked us whether we had food. Nobody mistreated us. My children or my husband. They even always asked what we might need. So I don't know what else we could have wished for. In these times, you see our apartment was inspected but nothing, not one glass, was broken. Everything was normal, regularly. They checked neatly. I don't know who could state such things, and there was also Dr. Hadzic. Now, he's over in Zgon with his mother because she's on her deathbed. He's over there with his mother and family. No one ever touched him. So as far as we are concerned, we have been together for several days -- he left because his mother is sick. Does this mean that the Serbs treated loyal Muslims, that is, decent citizens of Muslim ethnicity correctly and according to plan? Absolutely. Yes, absolutely. As far as I have access, and I think I have, I have nothing to say. As far as I have heard, everything was correct and decent. I'm telling you, not a hair went missing from his head. We came across another one for whom Sarajevo TV claims that he is in the nether world at the Kljuc stadium. I'm referring to Dr. Emir Kapetanovic. What I have to say is that I, my brother, Nermin, and my family are safe and sound. Nobody from the authorities has harassed us, nobody bothered us, arrested us, nor summoned us to the SUP, probably because they had no cause to do so. I have nothing else to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Otherwise I don't have go often to town --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to point out what I said a moment ago, that these were stage-managed clips on Television Banja Luka. Here Kapetanovic is playing a basketball match in days when people were not allowed to walk around. The very next day he appeared in the Manjaca concentration camp. Therefore, Television Banja Luka and that of the ARK needed to show that the gynaecologist Emir Kapetanovic was sound and safe, and the next day he appeared in Manjaca. As for Dr. Zubcevic, the previous one, the dentist, he's ashamed of what he stated then. To this day he has not come to Kljuc. That's as much as I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] I am a gynaecologist by profession. My practice was out of town. But your practice is in the area where there was conflict. My practice was out of town. I moved there due to circumstances because I could not afford to pay rent in town. It was in the zone of war operations, and alas, it was hit. The practice does not exist any more. The bottom line is a lot has been destroyed. They told me at the SUP to report the damage, which is normal, as all other citizens. I hope that of course something will be repaired and I'll be able to buy something. The current authorities know what was involved and what to do about it. All these lies in Kljuc municipality exist and persevere thanks to the fact that the Muslim extremists have managed to put out of action the repeater in Ramici so that the best part of the municipality cannot follow the TV programme. The only exception is the part towards Ribnik which receives the broadcast from Mrkonjic Grad. Therefore, an appeal from Kljuc that the relay be repaired as soon as possible and that Banja Luka helps them. How is the information in this area otherwise? Already before the aforementioned conflicts in Kljuc on the 27th of May this year, the Muslim extremists carried out an act of sabotage at the repeater in the village of Ramici so that most of the people of Kljuc could not receive broadcasts from any TV centre. That is one problem. The other is that Radio Kljuc has very poor reception throughout the municipality so that the citizens of Kljuc could not always and in time receive necessary information. This problem became even more complicated when the electricity was cut. Namely, in the last ten days Kljuc has poor electricity supply, so that Radio Kljuc could not perform the role in informing the Kljuc public during the war operations that it should have had. The next problem that was present in the last ten days was the problem of telephone connections with the world. Namely, we had no telephone connections with Banja Luka and the connections with Prijedor were rather poor. Also, bus lines were disrupted so that we could not receive the press from any part of the republic and the other republics of Yugoslavia. Regarding the arming of the Muslims in Kljuc municipality, it is well known who participated and how. Let us only mention that the main suppliers were Teufik Vukcic, a plumber, and a Romany by the name of Zijo from Curcici, the owner of a cafe, a boutique, and a goldsmith shop. A big friend of Nihad Durakovic, the former president of the League of Communists of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Zijo is one of the wealthier people in Kljuc and is now hiding in Vienna where he also has another company. At the end of this block about the war, we should like to point out the heroes of the Serbian defenders. We should like to mention the fearlessness and courage of Nikola Vracar, professor at the Lazar Djukic high school centre, who performed a real heroic deed and saved the life of several comrades by skilfully and timely throwing a grenade when he and his comrades were ambushed. Unfortunately not the life of Dusan Dule Stojakovic, assistant commander of the public security station from Kljuc who was killed by the Muslims. What is the assessment of the political security situation now? The political security situation in Kljuc is quite complicated. We feel free to say that in the last ten days the situation has improved somewhat, that it is calming down. One may say that life is being normalised and we will try to secure normal life and work throughout the municipality in the future, including economic and public institutions which will start functioning normally. Let me ask you frankly, do you think that it is possible after all these events for Muslims and Serbs to live together in your municipality? Generally it is difficult to answer this question. I think that life has to be totally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] -- ethnically demarcated and the areas --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we see from what Jovo Banjac is saying that already in advance they had preconceived the resettlement of peoples and the commission of genocide. From what he says, you will see that he's suggesting the resettlement of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] And the areas cleansed from all those who cannot live together in this area. Is this better done by war or peacefully? In my opinion the only solution would be a peaceful one, never by war. I think that we haven't -- don't have much influence on this, since small communities like Kljuc. I think that the leadership of the level of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the former Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, together with the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina have to do this job, and we will do everything at our level, at the municipal -- at the level of the municipalities belonging to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We should do what is necessary. If I understood you correctly, this means that Karadzic in the first place and the government of the Serbian Republic, should find a solution in talks with Alija Izetbegovic, with Boban, in this case, with Izetbegovic, because it concerns the Muslims of your municipality. I think that is the only situation. If this solution is not achieved, I'm afraid that the situation will become worse because the war is not over yet. The war continues and can easily turn into a war up to the extermination of one or other people. It is important in all this to point out that the parties of Kljuc municipality signed peace agreements, but MBO, SDA, and the liberals secretly prepared for war. This is best illustrated by the fact that at the session of the municipality council of parliamentary parts on the 14th of May in discussing the current political situation, it was established that the situation was difficult but that there were no pronounced inter-ethnic conflicts. I quote, "Because in this area no existence of any paramilitary formations such as the Green Berets or White Eagles or similar had been noticed." And only ten days after that, the armed conflict broke out. Storage depots were found, trenches dug by the Green Berets in Velagici, Pudin Han, Krasulje, and other villages with Muslim population. Several days before our visit the last group of refugees returned from Kljuc to Slavonia from the area of the town on the Sana River where they had stayed for several months and found shelter in the tourist hotel with the families of many Kljuc citizens. Leaving Kljuc on the banks of the clear and full of fish Sana River behind us in Kljuc, only stayed the Serbian flag made by Ljubica Amidzic from Rudenice to wave, which the Muslim extremists tried to tear down several times but were prevented. We went to Gornji Ribnik to visit the fish farm. The traffic blockade also affects the fish because there is less food. We are faced with a fait accompli because there is no substitute for fish feed produced in the veterinarian institute in Zemun and Padinska Skela. We tried to combine some products, adding vitamin components to lessen the disaster we are faced with and to save what we can. The current situation is devastating for the reasons given above. However, we have engaged all available means to try to offer a quantity of fish on a market in the Banja Luka region so as to mitigate the disaster, which we expect to occur in a couple of days. The reasons are clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fast-forward to where.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we fast-forward past this. We'll see a subtitle "Business working again." And then we'll see Mr. Dakic apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's it. Stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can we just identify him as well before we move on with the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. We can go on. I just want the picture of the man with the -- yes, stop, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, that is ...?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tihomir Dakic. Dakic, vice-president of the executive board. He was a member of the Crisis Staff as opposed to the others. He's the only one in civilian clothes, all the others in uniforms, military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that -- unless my learned friends -- Defence counsel want this played, it's about the economy. If we could -- we could perhaps fast-forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you interested, Mr. Ackerman, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can perhaps fast-forward this as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There's only one part we should come to. I don't know how difficult it is to find it. About the economic -- well, Your Honour, perhaps we can leave it. The transcripts going to be made an exhibit. And the rest is really about economy. So perhaps we can leave the video there. Thank you. Your Honour, all that -- what is said, and I draw Your Honours' attention to page 19 of the transcript. In respect of the connection with Serbia. Your Honour, we've had the video made an exhibit but not the transcripts. So could I ask -- the video was made P1100. Could I ask perhaps that the English version of the transcript be P1100.1A and the B/C/S .1B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] So it will be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Let's deal immediately, Mr. Filipovic, with Mr. Kapetanovic, although I was going to come to these documents a little later. Could you be shown, please, Exhibit 1033.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] This is in which --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's in volume 2. Your Honour, you will need to look for this in the B/C/S. Because it's a list of names, only the introduction and a few of the names were translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a letter being sent from Kljuc to Banja Luka CSB dated the 29th of August, and it states: "Pursuant to your dispatch, we are sending you the following information: There are no camps, prisons, or collection centres in our municipality. We send all prisoners to the Manjaca prisoner of war camp at Dobrinja and we cannot provide information in respect to the request." Now, "In reference to item 4, please find enclosed a list of all prisoners from the Kljuc municipality." Now, it starts at number 1 and ends at 1.163. Can we look at number 131, please. Is that you, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then if we go to the very last page. 1161.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Kapetanovic Emir. As I said a moment ago, he did his bit. He appeared in the programme. And then he came to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By this date in August I think your brother was dead, but is that -- is that his name at 1162?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. They wanted to cover it up, to say that Omer was not in Manjaca at all. And upon the insistence of the International Red Cross, we insisted that Omer's name be entered because he was registered with the International Red Cross and we requested that his name be included in the list. And I can tell Their Honours that the Serbian authorities issued a medical report saying that Omer had died of natural causes, which is a mere lie. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then next, please, I want you to look at a document that's not in the bundle as yet, Your Honour. It's one of the documents that we copied. It's the criminal report of the 9th of June, 1995. It was in that extra bundle we added. It's dated the 9th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do Your Honours have your -- were you given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Since it hasn't got a number, it will be difficult to trace it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is one of the reasons I keep on saying we're not going to hand them out to you in advance, because it's easier if we give them to you at the time. I think the easiest thing is to put the first page onto the ELMO and -- no. It looks like this. It says -- it's headed "Republika Srpska. Ministry of the Interior. Prijedor public security centre. Public security station Kljuc."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I just get a copy from you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, you can't because we handed out specifically -- this is the one copy I have and we handed them out specifically so that they're there and available. All right. We have got another copy here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How does it start?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's headed, Your Honour -- it's 03037541, "Republika Srpska, Ministry of the Interior --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. That's it. Thank you. And we've handed out an extra copy again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as requested to -- whatever it was, the day before Mr. Filipovic gave evidence, we handed over copies of a number of documents. But anyhow, Your Honour, I'm going to ask a few questions about it. But may this now be made Prosecutor's Exhibit 110 -- yes, 1101.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In June of 1995, not so long before Dayton, I suppose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is being numbered?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is. 1101, Your Honour, 1101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And the transcript of the video being ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 1100.1A and B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in June of 1995, Mr. Filipovic, were you made aware that the public prosecutor in Kljuc was filing a criminal report against you and a number of other people?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't be aware because I had been expelled from my town, so that in 1995 I was living in London.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So there was no contact with you in London to inform you that you were apparently with some dead people about to be prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When did you first find out that these charges had been filed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned to Kljuc. When I returned there, this document was in the police station, so that I was made aware of it, that I came under number 8, charged -- that I was charged. And this could have held water if they had waited for Dayton. But before Dayton, they were illegal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You were not born on the 27th of January, 1955. You were born on the 27th of October.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But my father's name is Sule and my mother's name is Aisa. So it's a typing error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can we look at number 1 there please, on the list. Your brother, at that stage well and truly dead and buried is being charged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 2, Mr. Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Emir Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same Emir Kapetanovic who was in Manjaca and who we saw on that video?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the dentist, Omer -- the one -- the one we saw on the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he's not on this list because he had done his bit in another way. After his statement, the Serbs put him on a convoy and deported him. This same gentleman is now living in America.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all, some 239 people are charged. And the charges are that on grounds of reasonable suspicion of having committed the gravest form of the crime of armed rebellion. And I'm not going to go through the description, because effectively it just covers the same ground as the events you've already dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should add -- I think this document was supplied to us as a result of a request to the authorities in the RS. I may be wrong. Because I think we were asked for the attachments, and all that was supplied was a copy of the criminal report. And we don't have the things that were -- it says at the end "Attachments in evidence."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Actually, it was the Defence who requested the attachments.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under the Rule 68. And these attachments according to our information are with the municipal court in Kljuc, and this is not Republika Srpska. It's Federation right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, well, then -- yes, Your Honour, that's quite right. But you're -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, it's quite right. And we were asked for the copies of the attachments, but all we were supplied with was this, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And -- I stand corrected, of course it's Kljuc, so it's the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all I want to ask about that document. Thank you very much, Mr. Filipovic. Now, Mr. Filipovic, I just, I think, want to ask you about a couple of other documents and then I'll come to your arrest and incarceration in Manjaca. And if I may just find my list of documents. Now, Mr. Filipovic, I'd like you to be shown on the same topic of the events in Kljuc, please --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, P967, please. And that's in volume 2. P967 in volume 2. It should be after -- if the dividers are the same as mine, divider 47 in the beginning. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document that has been objected to in specific terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a diary apparently, Mr. Filipovic, that was recovered. And it's got a name on it, on the front -- on the inside, I think, of the front cover, which is Ilija Buvac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him personally. He is currently living in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a list apparently on the front page of various people who are related to him. Again, do you recognise those as his relations?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buvac Ilija. Darinka Buvac, that's his wife. Drago Buvac, son. Dimitar Buvac, son, who was investigator of the Serb police. Svetozar Buvac, son. Dragica Buvac, daughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanija Buvac, daughter, but she died a long time ago. Her nickname was Seka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. I just want you to identify them as you know them. Now, I just want to ask you about a few entries. Apparently, this gentleman kept a diary during the time of these events. If we go to the entry for Thursday, the 28th of May, so the day of your arrest. He states that at around 1800, so at that time you were definitely on your way to Stara Gradiska I think, "An attack was carried out on Kljuc from the -- from various hill sectors and the army and the TO of the Serbian Republic of Bosnian Krajina repulsed the attack an hour later." You told us about this time you were being carted off to Stara Gradiska. Do you remember anything about an attack?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spoke -- I mentioned this early on. At about 5.30 p.m. we were taken out, and then the shooting began from the direction of the hospital and from the direction of Hamlovici. There could be no question of an attack because here it says that in the city there is not a soul except for the army and the police. So in other words, no attack could have taken place from the direction of the hospital, because the hospital is in the town. And when we were exposed it was said that the balijas were attacking the hospital. And we were ordered to return. We were in the corridor then. The shooting started, and that at about 6.00 p.m. the shooting ended. We were loaded onto trucks and taken to Stara Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then the only other matter about this diary that I want to ask you about is this: There's an entry for Saturday, the 30th of May, 1992. There's something about -- somebody called Ibro Adzamovic from Rejzovici was killed on the street even though he had not participated in combat. And then it states: "Today Omer Filipovic, commander of the Kljuc Green Beret Army, Municipal Staff (Muslims), surrendered in Kljuc to the military forces of the Serbian Republic of the Bosnia-Herzegovina." And was that right, he did surrender on that day, the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he surrendered on the 29th. But perhaps I was informed later. But to the best of my knowledge, I think it was on the 29th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned the killing of Ibro Adzamovic. And it was said that he was killed although he had not taken part in combat. He was killed in the very centre of Kljuc, near the house of Cedo Acimovic, so there's no question of a front line being there. And in the report of the public security station it was said that this person had been killed on the front line. And at the home of Cedo Acimovic on the Marsal Tito Street, there is no front line. It is in the very centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Filipovic, we come now to - because you've mentioned a number of times - your arrest. I don't think we can finish it this afternoon, but perhaps you can start. What happened to you on the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On May 28th, 1992, as I have already stated, a neighbour informed me that on Radio Kljuc it was demanded that I should surrender, me and my brother. I said that I had no reason to surrender and if they needed me, they should come and fetch me. And I went home. I saw my wife was nervous and panicky. I asked her what happened, and she told me that the police and the military were there, that they had searched the house. I walked into the house. We have -- we see that there was -- I saw that everything was tumbled. They took -- my wife told me that they had taken the pistol and Radenko Ciric, a policeman who was calmer and more civilised than the others, he told my wife, "Madam, it would be good for him to come because someone might kill him if they see him walking around." And she said, "Why should you kill him?" And then someone with an accent, the Ekavica accent, who said that he was Kragujevac told my wife, "Call him." And my wife refused because she said, "I don't even call my children, let alone my husband. He must be around the house somewhere." And then they left, but they left an ambush of two persons on my land. My school friend who used to sit in the same desk with me, Radojcic Ratko and Radenko. And since it was the end of May, there was very high grass. They were lying in the grass, and I didn't notice them. Before that my sister-in-law asked me to see what had happened to her house because my sister-in-law and her children were in my house, and our houses are about 30 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we pause there, Mr. Filipovic. Can we come directly to what happened at the time you were actually arrested.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment I went -- when I found out what happened in my sister-in-law's house, I went to my garden, about 30 or 40 metres away. And two people jumped in front of me and they said, "Put up your hands. Surrender." And I did not wish to put up my hands. I thought I had nothing to surrender for. "I know both of you, Rade. We used to be neighbours." His house was 100 metres from mine and we used to share the same desk in the seventh grade of elementary school. He told me, "Give me your ID. Who are you?" And I said, "I knew many things before, but the fact that you have lost your memory so fast, don't you remember that we used to share a desk?" "Your ID." Then Ratko Radojcic said, "Muhamed give him the ID because he's heading the patrol and he might just do anything." I was angry. I threw the ID at him. It hit him on his chest and it fell onto the ground. Then he read through it. He asked who my father was. I then understood the situation. I said, "I have no idea who my father is." And he answered, "I don't know. You know very well who my father is, so I don't want to answer that question." And then I was taken away. And I remained alive thanks to Ratko Radojcic at that moment, who -- he -- well, he could not forget years of friendship, that he didn't want me to be hit by a sniper shot. But my -- since my home is not on the main road -- going out onto the main road, I went 10 metres in front of the two of them and then we -- when we arrived to Musa Music's house, then Rade said, "Let him go." I stopped and Ratko ran up to me and said, "Muhamed, you're an officer. You know how to march. Stand by my right side." I didn't even think of this until I came across this tape. And then I realised that I was to have been shot. But since I was from Ratko's right side, I was not shot from Ratko's house. At the post office we reached -- we turned to the left. We reached the police station. And near the Orthodox church I saw uniformed Serb soldiers, policemen. I don't know what they were. And at the moment when I appeared there, at the same time everyone said, "Here is the leading Turk."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we deal with that. At the police station, people -- officers said, "Here is --" or uniformed men said, "Here is the leading Turk."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you treated at that stage?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just let me finish. Before I came to the stairs of the police building, I came across a guards post. Bajic -- I don't know his real name. I know his surname is Bajic. Bajic, he used to work at the post office, and he told me, "See how beautiful it is. Kiss it." He was referring to the Serb flag. I refused. "Let your father kiss it. I won't." And I used that opportunity to be protected by Ratko, because Ratko stood in front of him and told him not to touch me. So that was the second moment when I was saved. From that point to the staircase of the police, there were about 15 or 20 metres. Here Ratko could not save me, and a whole crowd of people approached me. They hit him [as interpreted]. They said -- Ratko said, "I have to reach Vinko." And the rest of them said, "Well, fuck Vinko." I only remember falling unconscious. And I saw from the window of the priest's home that I saw the priest looking behind the curtain, and then I just thought that if Muhamed were to die in about 15 or 20 years, one would find out how he died. And what I remember is that I came to in the office of Todo Gajic, the investigator, and he -- and the beating started at 10.30 until 5.30, and I believe as far as I could count I lost consciousness seven or eight times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think we'll have to leave what happened in the office until tomorrow. But two things: The interpreter said that "they hit him" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "They hit him."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- which could be -- when you were being hit outside the police station, I'm sorry, who was being hit outside the police station?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I know it seems mad, but we have to get this right for the translation. How many roughly were outside the police station and beating you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least 50. And I only know one of them. I was able to recognise one of them, Dusan Sladojevic, who was a driver, a bus driver in Kljuc. I recognised him because; the others I didn't, because the tactics with the Serbs was that Kljuc went to other towns, to Sanski Most, and people from Sanski Most would come to Kljuc, so that the victims could not recognise their executors. I remembered Sladojevic Dusan -- Dusan Sladojevic. And I thought at the moment that we would meet in court, that there would be a rule of law some day in this country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they were beating you, what were they using? Any instruments or just hands and feet?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Feet, fists, rifles, and nearby Kljuc there was a factory of furniture, a furniture factory. And legs of chairs were used that were in fact worked on. Not like baseball bats but -- so they used these legs of chairs, army boots, rifle butts, whatever they could get their hands on. Lizija [phoen] in the office even put a bomb in my mouth, a knife under my throat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just one final question: When you were originally looking at the town plan of Kljuc and you identified the police station with the flight of stairs -- you'd said you'd been thrown down a flight of stairs. Did that happen then or later?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th at about 5.30 -- between 5.30 and 6.00. I think it was closer to 6.00 that I was thrown down the stairs. It was about 6.00, 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was as you were being taken out of the building.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My hands were tied on my back, and I fell down the stairs like a sack of cement to the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Filipovic. That brings us to the end of our work for today. We will continue tomorrow, at the same time, 2.15, this same courtroom. I thank you. Have a nice evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.31 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of September, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 25
